verdict.rationale: Rippling's own product pages describe user-defined dynamic rules and custom workflows that fire automatically on events. Examples include role changes updating access, offboarding triggering device retrieval, and security threats triggering notifications. However, all of this is marketing-level claimed documentation with no detail on how rules are authored, so the depth of event-triggered automation is unproven. missing for 10: documentation of the rule/workflow builder (available triggers, conditions, action types), any programmatic or AI-native way to define the rules, and independent or hands-on corroboration that custom event-triggered rules work as claimed.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: You define the rules, Rippling runs the rest.
dynamic rules automatically ensure the right people get the right level of access—even as their roles change
The instant an employee is offboarded in Rippling, AI triggers the retrieval flow and generates the shipping label, dispatches the box, and tracks the return.
Custom workflows will automatically notify you of any security threats
When roles changes or someone leaves, Rippling automatically updates access, permissions, and groups.
Build and enforce custom security policies based on hundreds of user and device attributes.
